decisions.rationale: Cataracts is a named ocular disease, the phenotype developed by the Six5-deficient mice, and it has a single specific definition.
Myotonic dystrophy is a named specific disease with a single definition.
DM1 is the disease name (myotonic dystrophy type 1) used to modify the noun 'locus', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
Myotonic dystrophy is named as the disease caused by the CTG repeat expansion, a specific disease.
'Dominantly inherited disease' describes a family of diseases defined by inheritance pattern rather than one specific disease, like the 'autosomal recessive disease' example.
Skeletal muscle dystrophy refers to a family of muscular dystrophies rather than one specific disease.
Myotonia is a named clinical disease entity with a single definition, a feature of myotonic dystrophy.
Cataracts is a named specific ocular disease with a single definition.
Cardiac conduction defects denotes a family of cardiac conduction disorders (multiple specific conduction diseases), so it is a Disease Class.
Myopathy is a family of muscle diseases encompassing multiple specific disorders.
Cardiac conduction abnormalities names a category of conduction disorders; the cardiac conduction qualifier makes it a class rather than the excluded general term 'abnormalities' alone.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Disease Class); What NOT to Annotate §4 (general terms)

decisions.rationale: Myotonic dystrophy is a named specific disease with a single definition, referred to as a feature set.
Myotonia is a named clinical disease entity with a single definition.
Cataracts is a named specific ocular disease with a single definition.
Like the 'C7 deficiency' example, 'SIX5 deficiency' names a specific genetic deficiency condition causing the cataract phenotype, not a general term.
'Myotonic dystrophy' is used to modify the noun 'phenotype' and so is annotated as a Modifier.
Lenticular opacities denotes the specific lens disease (cataract) manifestation developed by the mice.
'SIX5 deficiency' is a specific genetic deficiency condition, analogous to 'C7 deficiency', and is not a general term.
'Cataract' modifies the noun 'phenotype' and is therefore annotated as a Modifier.
Myotonic dystrophy is a named specific disease used as the disease in which the cataract phenotype occurs.
Myotonic dystrophy is a named specific disease with a single definition.
'Multigenic disorder' refers to a family of disorders defined by multigene causation rather than one specific disease.
